description: We are a group of three high school students passionate about coding, space and entrepreneurship.
summary: iso-topos is a 3D app matching Moon & Mars targets to 89,022 Earth H3 cells and 26 hotspots across 17 physical parameters using NASA PDS & open data—exposing unit deltas and Earth-limit caveats.
details:
iso-topos helps planetary scientists, mission planners, and robotics teams systematically identify and evaluate Earth analog sites for lunar bases, lunar landing sites, and Mars exploration targets. Users can pick from 12 curated Moon and Mars mission presets (such as Shackleton Crater Rim, Mons Mouton Plateau, Aristarchus Plateau, Mare Tranquillitatis Skylight Pit, Arcadia Planitia, Jezero Crater Delta, and Oxia Planum) or click any coordinate on an interactive 3D Moon or Mars globe (/planetary) to extract local target parameters and rank matching terrestrial regions.

An offline open-data pipeline pre-aggregates global Earth, Moon, and Mars grids into lightweight GeoJSON and JSON indices so the browser never parses raw GeoTIFF, NetCDF, HDF5, or PDS rasters. The terrestrial index pairs 89,022 uniform H3 Resolution-4 hexagons (roughly 26 km edge length, spanning land and Antarctic ice shelves with antimeridian and polar splitting) with 26 local hotspots covering sub-grid features such as calcic anorthosite outcrops, lava tubes, ice caves, impact craters, and evaporite basins. A vectorized NumPy scoring engine evaluates all candidates across 17 physical parameters in 5 dimensions—Topography and Terrain; Geology, Mineralogy, and Magnetism; Temperature and Illumination; Water, Ice, and Permafrost; and Subsurface, Biology, and Operations—in under 100 ms. In Simple Mode, users explore interactive 3D and 2D CesiumJS globes, inspect dimension breakdowns, and enable "Beyond Well-Known Sites" to dim classic test hubs (Antarctica, Atacama, Iceland, Hawaii, Haughton, and Rio Tinto) and surface under-studied analogs such as White Mountain in Greenland, Lake Salda, Batagaika, and Grotta del Gelo. Advanced Mode unlocks per-parameter overrides, 0–100% weight sliders with N/A handling when dimensions are disabled, Clamped versus Strict Physical Distance scoring, physical range filters, full provenance tables, and CSV or JSON export.

Because no terrestrial site replicates spaceflight environments completely, every result displays explicit Earth-Limit Caveats alongside similarity metrics, detailing gaps including 0.165 g lunar and 0.38 g Martian gravity, lunar hard vacuum versus convective air, 6 mbar Martian CO2 atmosphere, unshielded radiation, pitch-black lunar shadows, and vacuum or low-pressure ice sublimation versus melting. Modeling limits are surfaced transparently in dataset provenance: 0–5 degree grazing sunlight hours rely on an analytical solar ephemeris without cloud cover or local horizon masking, orbital thermal and ice metrics combine NASA PDS grids with radiometric latitude models, global GLiM lithology serves as a macro proxy complemented by sub-grid hotspots, and missing track gaps such as those in EMAG2v3 are interpolated locally and flagged per cell.

The backend and offline ETL are built with Python 3.14, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, NumPy, h3, tifffile, h5py, and httpx, paired with a zero-build ES module frontend using CesiumJS, h3-js, and Chart.js under the MIT License.
